standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the integral element to a fraction over each local ring, where normality is the hypothesis available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of localisation for the total ring of fractions
standard_prerequisites.use: Places the total ring of fractions inside its localisation so that the fraction representation can be compared.

core_obligations: Let x be integral over R in the total ring of fractions and let I be the ideal of elements f with fx in R (proof lines 8440-8441).

For a prime p, use flatness of the localisation to compare the total ring of fractions with its localisation and use normality of the local ring to get f outside p with fx in R (proof lines 8442-8446).
Show that I is not contained in any prime, hence equals R, so x lies in R (proof lines 8447-8451).
proof_roadmap: Introduce the ideal of denominators of the integral element (proof lines 8440-8441).
Localise at primes to find a denominator outside each prime and conclude that the ideal is the whole ring (proof lines 8442-8452).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a normal ring is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions (statement lines 8434-8437). The proof does not use a determinant trick or the theory of integral closures of ideals: it introduces the ideal I of elements f with fx in R, localises at a prime, uses flatness of the localisation together with normality of the local ring to find a denominator outside that prime, and then concludes that I lies in no prime and hence equals R (proof lines 8439-8452). Passing from a prime-wise denominator to a global statement about the ideal I is the content, and the author writes the localisation step explicitly. H2.
